data.title: Tiny Undervalued Hardware Companions (2024)
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一些实用且便宜的电脑配件，如各种角度转换器、USB适配器、SATA转USB-C/A适配器等，帮助解决日常使用中的小问题。例如，RJ45角度适配器可以避免网线直接垂直伸出笔记本侧面，USB-C和USB-A角度适配器也有类似功能。此外，文章还提到SATA转USB适配器适用于硬盘克隆，USB-C与USB-A互转适配器可应对接口变化，以及小型WiFi或Bluetooth无线适配器方便添加无线功能。这些小工具大多价格低廉（约1-5美元），可在AliExpress等平台找到。尽管文章像是在为AliExpress做推广，但实际并非如此。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：各种科技配件和电缆的管理、使用及推荐

不同观点：
• blitzar：怀念曾经苹果的磁性充电器有直角设计，但这种技术似乎已经失传。
• EvanAnderson：认为RJ45双母 coupler（连接适配器）非常实用，尤其是在需要临时接入网络时，可以方便地恢复原状，且在电缆长度不足时可以通过短电缆连接延长使用。
• epakai：喜欢存储各种小适配器，并通过使用多层桌和粘贴式小抽屉来有效组织和存放这些配件，方便快速取用。
• _tom_：使用24格收纳盒来分类存放不同类型的电缆，以避免在大盒子中翻找。
• o11c：提醒大多数USB到SATA适配器不支持硬盘驱动器（HDD），仅支持固态硬盘（SSD），并推荐了一种多功能USB A到C的适配器电缆。
• citizenpaul：购买了Sennheiser HD560S耳机，并通过V-MODA的BoomPro Mic增强了麦克风功能，同时带音量调节的功能让他觉得非常实用。
• wesleyd：使用大型的16口电源条和强力魔术贴来整理桌下设备，并提到使用SATA适配器像磁带机一样备份数据。
• quailfarmer：建议添加便携式HDMI/VGA显示器，以便检查无头机器（headless machines）。
• analog31：推荐长电源线和带长线的插线板，特别适用于避免在某些安装环境中违反安全规定。
• nickphx：不信任AliExpress上的USB-C电缆或转换器，暗示可能存在质量问题。
• rbanffy：建议90度旋转的RJ-45公对公连接器可以方便组建类似RPi的集群。
• 7speter：提到Lightning到USB-C转换器可以让一些较新的iOS设备变成便携电脑，或者用NVMe作为额外存储。

补充讨论：
• 关于USB适配器的争议：o11c指出某些USB-to-SATA适配器不支持HDD，而nickphx则对AliExpress上的USB-C电缆质量表示不信任。
• 关于Ethernet连接的实用性：EvanAnderson和rbanffy都提到了RJ45连接器和适配器的实际应用，包括临时接入网络和组建集群的便利性。
• 关于电缆和适配器的便携性：nicbou和wesleyd强调了使用较短或可伸缩电缆以及便携式适配器在旅行和安装中的优势。
• 关于音频设备的改进：gavinray对带有音量调节功能的BoomPro Mic给予高度评价，认为这种设计应被广泛采用。

44333960.article_content:
After playing/working with computers for more then 25 years I started to appreciate small but handy valuable stuff – like adapters or handlers or … yeah – all kind of stuff. With many of them I did not even knew they existed until I find out about them – mostly accidentally or after long searching for some problem solution. Today I will share them with You – so maybe they will end up handy also for You.
… and while they make my life easier – they are mostly very cheap too.
The
Table of Contents
is below.
RJ45 Angle Adapters
RJ45 Angle Cable Adapters
RJ45 Join Adapters
SATA to USB-C or USB-A Adapters
Angle USB-C and USB-A Adapters
USB-A <=> USB-C Adapters
Tiny USB WiFi or Bluetooth Dongle
USB-C <=> Micro USB Adapter
USB-C <=> Laptops/Routers/5.5mmx2.5mm Adapters
Creative BT-W2 USB-A Bluetooth Adapter
External Microphone for SONY Headphones
Headphones Handle
Dual USB-C and USB-A Pendrive (SanDisk)
Tiny USB-A Hub
Quad USB-C / USB-A / Lightning / Micro USB Adapter with MicroSD Card Slot
Angle Power Adapters
C13/C14 Power Adapters with Additional C1/C2 or C5/C6 Sockets
HDMI 3in1 Switch with Remote Control
Cable Organizers
Mouse Jigger
FM Transmitter
Summary
The whole article can ‘feel’ like a sponsored entry for the
https://aliexpress.com
portal – but it is not – its just the most cheap place I was able to find these gems. Feel free to share even cheaper one if You have one.
~
RJ45 Angle Adapters
I mostly use laptops to do various tasks and cables sticking out on the sides perpendicularly does not help. Not many laptops today have the RJ45 LAN socket – but if they do – they are mostly on the side of the laptop.
Thanks to such angle RJ45 adapters it is no longer a problem.
You can find them for about
$2
– for example – on
https://aliexpress.com
page – with the
RJ45 ANGLE ADAPTER
keywords in their search.
~
RJ45 Angle Cable Adapters
The mentioned earlier
RJ45 Angle Adapters
are quite bulky – but as an alternative its possible to get a short 40cm cable with smaller plug.
Not sure if its noticeable on the picture below – but I also cut the top ‘cover’ with knife of the plug – so its easier to detach.
There are of course all four angles to choose from.
One may also use the end of that 40cm cable-adapter as a ‘stopper’ to not fall inside the desk hole as shown on the image below.
You can find them for about
$2
– for example – on
https://aliexpress.com
– with the
RJ45 ANGLE ADAPTER CABLE
keywords in their search.
~
RJ45 Join Adapters
Often I found myself in a situation that the currently available LAN cable was too short to reach and it needed a lot of work to plot another – longer one.
With these simple ‘join’ adapters it is no longer a problem. You would not use them in a serious Data Center with 10+ GE speeds – but for home 1.0-2.5 GE speeds its more then enough.
You can find them for about
$1-$2
– for example – on
https://aliexpress.com
– with the
RJ45 JOIN ADAPTER
keywords in their search.
~
SATA to USB-C or USB-A Adapters
Multiple times I needed to clone some old disk to new SSD – just to make an old system faster.
I usually boot from some USB drive with FreeBSD and while new SSD is attached with these adapters – I then execute
dd(8)
command to clone the old HDD disk to new SSD drive … and then just swap them out.
You can find them for about
$1-$5
– for example – on
https://aliexpress.com
– with the
SATA USB ADAPTER
keywords in their search.
~
Angle USB-C and USB-A Adapters
As we already talked about RJ45 angle adapters … there are also USB-C and USB-A angle adapters.
The do the same good job with cables to not stick out on a side of a laptop.
You can find them for about
$1-$3
– for example – on
https://aliexpress.com
– with the
ANGLE USB ADAPTER
keywords in their search.
~
USB-A <=> USB-C Adapters
In the progressing and always changing world yesterday the USB-A was king and tomorrow the USB-C will be.
There are multiple cases in which you will need these – from simple USB headphones to USB pendrives and other stuff.
You can find them for about
$1-$3
– for example – on
https://aliexpress.com
– with the
USB-C USB-A ADAPTER
keywords in their search.
~
Tiny USB WiFi or Bluetooth Dongle
Multiple times I have found myself in a situation where it was very convenient to just add some WiFi or Bluetooth chip over USB port and do the job instead of trying to achieve the same without such chips.
While I usually omit Bluetooth I can not say the same about WiFi … and as FreeBSD lacks a little in that department – using a very tiny chip such as
Realtek RTL8188CUS
often does the job done.
You can find them for about
$1-$3
– for example – on
https://aliexpress.com
– with the
WIFI USB
or
BLUETOOTH USB
keywords in their search.
~
USB-C <=> Micro USB Adapter
In the past – in the USB Micro times – I remember using an adapter to be able to charge – then new and uncommon – USB-C devices.

data.title: Learn you Galois fields for great good (2023)
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了有关抽象代数的系列内容，重点讲解伽罗瓦域（有限域）及其在计算机科学中的应用。作者提到，当前缺乏适合计算机科学家的学习资源，多数材料要么过于简化，要么假设读者具备纯数学背景。为此，作者计划通过循序渐进的方式，结合实际代码实现，填补这一空白。抽象代数关注数字间的关系而非数字本身，适用于数据编码、加密、纠错等领域。系列内容从基础理论开始，逐步介绍如Reed-Solomon、AES等应用，包含大量练习以帮助理解。尽管不要求太多数学背景，但某些应用需要线性代数知识。代码将采用Rust编写，注重可读性和教育性，而非性能优化。最终目标是为计算机科学家提供易于理解的参考实现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Galois域的构造及其与复数构造的类比，以及对代数教学和学习资源的讨论

不同观点：
• kasadkad认为Galois域的构造与复数的构造类似，通过添加一个“虚拟数”来扩展域，但需要选择不可约多项式以确保构造的有效性。他详细解释了如何通过选择适当的多项式来构造GF(4)，并指出了不同多项式的选择对构造的影响。
• nayuki提供了一些相关的解释资源链接，涵盖了群和域的内容，为读者提供了进一步学习的资料。
• tempodox强调了用简单语言解释复杂概念的重要性，引用了爱因斯坦的名言来支持这一观点。
• __rito__表达了对帖子的赞赏，认为内容精彩。
• JackFr指出了文章中关于域的闭包性质和多项式乘法约简步骤的缺失，提出了改进建议。
• revskill批评了代数教学中只给出定义而不解释原因的做法，认为这不利于学习。
• behnamoh提到文章使用了Rust语言，但个人偏好Haskell或Lean，并希望可视化内容能贯穿整个章节。
• graycat提供了关于抽象代数和Galois理论的经典教材推荐，并分享了个人学习经验，指出了一些在有限域中需要特殊证明的情况。
• gnabgib提供了一个存档链接，可能与讨论内容相关。
• m3kw9对标题的语法错误提出了批评。
• untitled2反驳了对计算机科学课程中缺少代数内容的抱怨，认为每所大学都提供数学作为辅修课程，质疑那些没有选择数学辅修的人的职业选择。

补充讨论：
• kasadkad的评论引发了对如何选择适当多项式来构造Galois域的深入讨论，并与复数的构造进行了类比。
• 不同读者对文章的细节和表达方式提出了不同看法，如JackFr对内容不完整的批评和tempodox对简单语言的强调。
• behnamoh和graycat的评论扩展了讨论范围，涉及编程语言偏好和经典教材推荐，丰富了学习资源的选择。
• untitled2对代数在计算机科学课程中的地位提出了不同的看法，引发了对课程设置的争议。

争议焦点：
• 代数教学中是否充分解释了定义的根源问题（revskill的观点）。
• 计算机科学课程中代数内容的设置是否合理（untitled2的观点）。
• 文章内容的完整性和表达方式是否足够清晰（JackFr和m3kw9的批评）。

Introduction
This is the introduction to a series on Abstract Algebra. In particular, our focus will be on Galois Fields (also known as Finite Fields) and their applications in Computer Science. This is a project I've been excited about for many years now, but have been too busy to dedicate the adequate effort to meet my perfectionism standards (yay perfectionism!).
Backstory
Many moons back I was self-learning Galois Fields for some erasure coding theory applications. I was quite disappointed with the lack of accessible resources for computer scientists.
Many resources assumed either:
Its beyond your skill level so let's oversimplify (
"it's hard, don't worry about it"
), or
You had prior Pure Math studies in Abstract Algebra (
"it's easy, just use jargon jargon jargon"
)
Unfortunately, Abstract Algebra is not standard subject matter in most computer science curriculums. Often computer science mathematics start and end
with Discrete Math. If you're lucky, maybe you've also been exposed to Linear Algebra.
So, ultimately, I ended up self-learning Abstract Algebra from a pure math textbook. But for the great majority of computer scientists, there has to be a better way.
This series intends to fill this gap. This is the gentle step-by-step approach with applications implemented with actual code. It's the intro I wanted when I was starting out.
What is this subject?
Abstract algebra is a beautiful subject. It's the idea that the numbers you're familiar with don't matter. The numbers are just
arbitrary labels. What matters is the relationships they have with other numbers when you add or multiply them. If the numbers
don't matter, then we can swap those labels for different labels and all the normal math rules will still work.
For example, we could create an algebra that allows us to add or multiply colors:
And this is what makes the subject abstract and confusing. How can you just say that numbers don't matter? It doesn't make sense.
And even so, why would we want to study this? Why would a computer scientist care?
Well, we use computer algorithms to manipulate data. We encode/decode it, we encrypt/decrypt it, we detect corruption, etc.
Wouldn't it be great if we could use normal math to do those things? Wouldn't it be great if would could add or multiply
an 8-bit byte by an 8-bit byte and get another 8-bit byte? And if we could do that, could we also do Linear Algebra over Data? Yes, yes, and more yes.
This is why studying Abstract Algebra is worthwhile.
(Hint: Neither 263 nor 9282 are answers, they are not 8-bit numbers)
You can also make quirky blog posts that make your friends think you've gone crazy, like
milk and cookies
🥛 🍪 😊
Applications
The applications and algorithms are staggering. You interact with implementations of abstract algebra everyday: CRC,
AES Encryption, Elliptic-Curve Cryptography, Reed-Solomon, Advanced Erasure Codes, Data Hashing/Fingerprinting, Zero-Knowledge Proofs, etc.
Having a solid-background in Galois Fields and Abstract Algebra is a prerequisite for understanding these applications.
Approach: Step-by-step, Active Learning, and Literate Programming
In this series, we will start from the very basics of theory and build up step-by-step to interesting applications such as Reed-Solomon,
AES, etc. As such, the material will be
very
cumulative. Many exercises will be included to aid understanding. Each section will build gradually,
but will assume mastery of the previous section. Active learning is
strongly encouraged
. We will expect that
readers are putting in adequate effort to grok the abstract concepts.
We won't assume too much mathematical background beyond high-school level algebra. However, in some applications (for example: Reed-Solomon),
familiarity with Linear Algebra will be required. We won't explain Linear Algebra since great resources already
exist
here
. You are encouraged to supplement as needed.
We will be including code in a Literate Programming style where appropriate.  For example, to aid understanding, we will build some interactive
command-line tools that allow you to play around with various theoretical concepts in practice. All code will be the
Rust Programming Language
, but advanced features will be intentionally avoided so that the code will be readable
by most experienced computer programmers.
The main goal of this series is understandability and education. As such, the implementations will not be optimal. We will forgo nearly all
optimizations you'd see in a production quality implementation: lookup-tables, vectorized instructions, clever representations, computer
architecture optimizations, etc. It's possible that later posts in the series will discuss optimizations, but this is not a primary goal. At the end,
we hope these implementations will serve as good reference implementations. This can have it's own merit since highly optimized al

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了由Chris Giles、Elie Diaz和Cem Yuksel开发的增强顶点块下降法（Augmented Vertex Block Descent, AVBD），这是一种快速、基于物理的模拟方法。AVBD具有无条件稳定性、高度并行化，并能收敛到隐式欧拉解。通过增强拉格朗日公式，该方法解决了硬约束和刚度比高的模拟难题，适用于复杂接触场景，包括刚体堆叠、摩擦、带有限制自由度的关节连接以及刚性与软体交互系统。其GPU并行实现可在低迭代次数下实现实时性能和稳定模拟。与现有方法相比，AVBD在处理复杂碰撞和约束方面表现出更好的性能、收敛性和稳定性。在线演示和论文视频提供了进一步的展示。

Augmented Vertex Block Descent (AVBD)
Augmented Vertex Block Descent (AVBD)
Chris Giles
Elie Diaz
Cem Yuksel
Vertex Block Descent is a fast physics-based simulation method that is unconditionally stable, highly parallelizable, and capable of converging to the implicit Euler solution. We extend it using an augmented Lagrangian formulation to address some of its fundamental limitations. First, we introduce a mechanism to handle hard constraints with infinite stiffness without introducing numerical instabilities. Second, we substantially improve the convergence in the presence of high stiffness ratios. These changes we introduce allow simulating complex contact scenarios involving rigid bodies with stacking and friction, articulated bodies connected with hard constraints, including joints with limited degrees of freedom, and stiff systems interacting with soft bodies. We present evaluations using a parallel GPU implementation that can deliver real-time performance and stable simulations with low iteration counts for millions of objects interacting via collisions, various joint/attachment constraints, and springs of various stiffness. Our results show superior performance, convergence, and stability compared to the state-of-the-art alternatives.

data.title: Unexpected security footguns in Go's parsers
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了Go应用程序中解析不可信数据带来的安全风险，特别是在JSON、XML和YAML解析器中的意外行为可能被攻击者利用，导致认证绕过、授权控制突破以及敏感数据泄露。文章通过三个攻击场景具体说明：

1. **(Un)Marshaling意外数据**：Go解析器可能暴露开发者本想保密的字段数据。
2. **解析器差异**：不同解析器处理相同输入的差异可能被利用来绕过安全控制。
3. **数据格式混淆**：解析器处理跨格式数据时可能产生可被利用的结果。

文章还列举了多个实际案例，并给出强化解析器配置的建议，包括如何应对Go标准库中的安全缺口。例如，使用结构体标签控制字段的序列化和反序列化行为，以及如何避免暴露敏感字段等。最后，文章总结了这些解析器的潜在安全问题和应对策略。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：解析和验证跨服务的一致性，特别是JSON和XML等数据格式在不同解析器中的行为差异，及其安全性和设计问题。

不同观点：
• **Joker_vD** 认为应通过使用相同的解析器或增加验证层（如strictJSONParse函数）来确保跨服务的一致性解析行为。同时建议"入口服务"不仅验证请求，还重新编码请求为有效格式。

• **bravesoul2** 质疑重用DTO（数据传输对象）并共享跨API的做法，指出这在Go语言中尤其奇怪，并批评JavaScript中不可避免的问题，如splats。

• **glenjamin** 指出，禁用未知字段会使API的前向和后向兼容性变得更加困难，而这通常是 desirable 的模式。

• **asimops** 认为不应将客户端原始数据转发给认证服务，强调“解析，而不是验证”的逻辑，并将其视为更安全的设计。

• **anitil** 对Go默认XML解析器接受前后垃圾数据感到惊讶，并指出即使是JSON这种看似简单的格式在现实世界中也有复杂性，如重复键的处理。

• **piinbinary** 赞扬文章的清晰度，同时对单一字符串能被解析为JSON、XML和YAML感到震惊。

• **octo888** 质疑在"创建用户"请求DTO中包含"IsAdmin"字段的合理性，建议为不同用途创建不同的数据模型，而不是直接映射到数据库行。

• **tptacek** 指出Go的`encoding/xml`不适合用于SAML实现，建议自行编写解析器，同时不推荐使用SAML。

• **aintnolove** 认为协议缓冲区能提供一致的序列化/反序列化体验，开始理解其吸引力。

• **e_y_** 作为非Go程序员，认为Go使用结构标签进行字段元数据定义相比Rust宏和Java注解显得落后。

• **fainpul** 建议通过将字段设为小写来使其私有，以防止外部访问（基于Go语言的特性）。

• **em-bee** 认为解析器不应负责过滤未知字段，数据验证应基于白名单，解析后的数据应仅包含需要的字段。

• **jerf** 强调这些问题并非Go独有，而是用户错误和JSON、XML本身固有的复杂性所致。指出处理重复键等问题没有“正确”方式，并提醒开发者在解析用户输入时要小心。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到JSON和XML解析的复杂性和潜在安全问题，尤其是在跨服务和跨语言的情况下。
• 对Go语言特定设计选择（如结构标签）的批评和解释，以及与其他语言特性（如Rust宏和Java注解）的比较。
• 对协议缓冲区等其他序列化/反序列化方案的提及，作为一致性和安全性的解决方案。

争议焦点：是否应在解析器中内置更多验证和保护机制，还是将这些责任交给应用程序逻辑。以及对不同语言和工具在处理JSON和XML等格式时的设计选择和安全性的讨论。

Page content
In Go applications, parsing untrusted data creates a dangerous attack surface that’s routinely exploited in the wild. During our security assessments, we’ve repeatedly exploited unexpected behaviors in Go’s JSON, XML, and YAML parsers to bypass authentication, circumvent authorization controls, and exfiltrate sensitive data from production systems.
These aren’t theoretical issues—they’ve led to documented vulnerabilities like
CVE-2020-16250
(a Hashicorp Vault authentication bypass found by Google’s Project Zero) and numerous high-impact findings in our client engagements.
This post contextualizes these unexpected parser behaviors through three attack scenarios that every security engineer and Go developer should understand:
(Un)Marshaling unexpected data
: How Go parsers can expose data that developers intended to be private
Parser differentials
: How discrepancies between parsers enable attackers to bypass security controls when multiple services parse the same input
Data format confusion
: How parsers process cross-format payloads with surprising and exploitable results
We’ll demonstrate each attack scenario with real-world examples and conclude with concrete recommendations for configuring these parsers more securely, including strategies to compensate for security gaps in Go’s standard library.
Below is a summary of the surprising behaviors we’ll examine, with indicators showing their security status:

Green
: Secure by default
🟠
Orange
: Insecure by default but configurable
🔴
Red
: Insecure by default with no secure configuration options

XML
YAML

encoding/json
version go1.24.1
encoding/xml
version go1.24.1
yaml.v3
version 3.0.1 (the most popular third-party Go YAML library)
We’ll use JSON in our following examples, but all three parsers have APIs equivalent to the ones we’ll see.
At their core, these parsers provide two primary functions:
Marshal
(serialize): Converts Go structs into their respective format strings
Unmarshal
(deserialize): Converts format strings back into Go structs
Go uses struct field tags to allow customization of how parsers should handle individual fields. These tags consist of:
A
key name
for serialization/deserialization
Optional
comma-separated directives
that modify behavior (e.g., the
omitempty
tag option tells the JSON serializer not to include the field in the JSON output string if it is empty)

io.Reader
interfaces rather than
byte

Sometimes, you need to limit which fields of a structure can be marshaled or unmarshaled.
Let’s consider a simple example in which a back-end server has an HTTP handler for creating users and another for retrieving that user after authentication.
When creating a user, you may not want the user to be able to set the
IsAdmin
field (i.e., unmarshal that field from the user input).
Similarly, when fetching the user, you may not want the user to return the user’s
Password

Fields without a tag

data.title: Scaling our observability platform by embracing wide events and replacing OTel
data.author: valyala
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者的内部观测平台如何从19 PiB增长到超过100 PB，处理近500万亿行数据，并成功应对了20倍事件量增长，同时CPU使用率减少到原来的10%以下。尽管OpenTelemetry（OTel）在初期有效，但随着数据规模和复杂性的增加，OTel成为瓶颈。为此，作者开发了自定义管道（SysEx），以更好地满足高性能需求，并引入了基于ClickHouse的HyperDX，提供更高效的观测体验。最终，作者转向ClickStack，这是一个围绕ClickHouse构建的端到端观测堆栈，旨在提升数据探索和根因分析的效率。文章总结了在大规模数据场景下，OTel的局限性和自定义解决方案的必要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：日志数据的可观测性、存储、压缩及相关工具技术的优缺点

不同观点：
• Xcelerate认为可以通过优化压缩算法进一步减少日志数据的存储量，特别是通过类似低秩张量分解等高级压缩技术。他对当前的压缩技术是否已达极限表示怀疑。
• b0a04gl指出，存储100PB的日志表明我们尚未明确哪些日志值得记录，建议通过自动修剪未查看日志或未查询日志来优化存储，称之为“注意力加权保留”。
• jurgenkesker认为该讨论仅与从Clickhouse收集日志相关，对其他日志来源不具 relevance。
• mrbluecoat强调OpenTelemetry在服务故障状态下仍能捕获日志的优势，而SysEx无法做到这一点。
• iw7tdb2kqo9对ClickHouse在大规模日志数据查询中的优势表示疑问，并询问为何不将日志数据存储为JSON文件。
• jappgar批评观测性最大化是一种“富人”的追求，暗示其不切实际或浪费资源。
• the_arun关心日志的保留时间，并质疑在x个月后是否还需要原始数据。
• atemerev对Clickhouse和Postgres在数据导入速度上的差异表示震惊。
• henning指出，广泛事件记录会大幅增加存储成本，而这一成本常被忽视。
• the_real_cher好奇Clickhouse和Dynamo使用的技术是否只是大型哈希表。
• revskill批评行业标准多为半成品或进行中的项目，导致生态系统分割，并认为这是一种试错过程，不合理。
• Thaxll认为如果服务宕机时无法获取日志，整个解决方案就无用。
• ofrzeta主张减少数据生成量，认为当前的做法是浪费。
• tjungblut总结，Clickhouse实现了零拷贝的原始字节操作，而不是JSON的编组和解组。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于日志数据存储和查询的效率问题，部分人认为当前技术已经足够，而其他人则相信仍有改进空间。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是对不同工具（如Clickhouse、ElasticSearch、Postgres）在大规模数据处理中的表现和适用性的比较。
• 数据压缩技术的潜力也是一个讨论热点，部分参与者认为高级压缩技术尚未被充分利用。
• 最后，关于日志数据的价值和存储策略（如自动修剪和注意力加权保留）的讨论反映了在实际应用中的不同需求和优先级。

Back
Blog
/
Engineering
Scaling our Observability platform beyond 100 Petabytes by embracing wide events and replacing OTel
Rory Crispin
Jun 19, 2025
-
32
minutes read
TLDR
#
Observability at scale:
Our internal system grew from 19 PiB to 100 PB of uncompressed logs and from ~40 trillion to 500 trillion rows.
Efficiency breakthrough:
We absorbed a 20× surge in event volume using under 10% of the CPU previously needed.
OTel pitfalls:
The required parsing and marshalling of events in OpenTelemetry proved a bottleneck and didn’t scale - our custom pipeline addressed this.
Introducing HyperDX:
ClickHouse-native observability UI for seamless exploration, correlation, and root-cause analysis with Lucene-like syntax.
Introduction
#
About a year ago, we
shared the story of LogHouse
- our internal logging platform built to monitor ClickHouse Cloud. At the time, it managed what felt like a massive 19 PiB of data. More than just solving our observability challenges, LogHouse also saved us millions by replacing an increasingly unsustainable Datadog bill. The response to that post was overwhelming. It was clear our experience resonated with others facing similar struggles with traditional observability vendors and underscored just how critical effective data management is at scale.
A year later, LogHouse has grown beyond anything we anticipated and is now storing over 100 petabytes of uncompressed data across nearly 500 trillion rows. That kind of scale forced a series of architectural changes, new tools, and hard-earned lessons that we felt were worth sharing - not least that OpenTelemetry (OTel) isn’t always the panacea of Observability (though we still love it), and that sometimes custom pipelines are essential.
In our case, this shift enabled us to handle a 20x increase in event volume using less than 10% of the CPU for our most critical data source - a transformation with massive implications for cost and efficiency.
Other parts of our stack have also changed, not least due to the
ClickHouse acquisition of HyperDX
. Not only did this give us a first-party ClickHouse-native UI, but it also led to the
creation of ClickStack
- an opinionated, end-to-end observability stack built around ClickHouse. With HyperDX, we’ve started transitioning away from our Grafana-based custom UI, moving toward a more integrated experience for exploration, correlation, and root cause analysis.
As more teams adopt ClickHouse for observability and realize just how much they can store and query affordably, we hope these insights prove as useful as our first post. If you’re curious about this journey, when and where OTel is appropriate, and how we scaled a log pipeline to 100PB…read on.
Get started today
Interested in seeing how ClickHouse works on your data? Get started with ClickHouse Cloud in minutes and receive $300 in free credits.
Sign up
Beyond general purpose: evolving observability at scale
#
Over the past year, our approach to observability has undergone a significant transformation. We've continued to leverage OpenTelemetry to gather general-purpose logs, but as our systems have scaled, we began to reach its limits. While OTel remains a valuable part of our toolkit, it couldn't fully deliver the performance and precision we needed for our most demanding workloads. This prompted us to develop purpose-built tools tailored to our critical systems and rethink where generic solutions truly fit. Along the way, we've broadened the range of data we collect and revamped how we present insights to engineers.
A new frontier of scale
#
When we last wrote about LogHouse, we were proud to handle 19 PiB of uncompressed data across 37 trillion rows. Today, those numbers feel like a distant memory. LogHouse now stores over 100 petabytes of uncompressed data, representing nearly 500 trillion rows.
Here's a quick look at the breakdown:
System
Uncompressed Size
Stored rows
SysEx
93.6 PB
431 Trillion
OTel
14.5 PB
16.7 Trillion
These numbers also tell a story. In our original post, 100% of our telemetry flowed through OpenTelemetry, with every log line collected via the same general-purpose pipeline. But as the scale and complexity of our data grew, so did the need for specialization.
While our total volume has grown more than 5x, the breakdown reveals a deliberate shift in strategy: today, the vast majority of our data comes from “SysEx”, a new purpose-built exporter we developed to handle high-throughput, high-fidelity system logs from ClickHouse itself. This shift marks a turning point in how we think about observability pipelines - and brings us to our first key topic.
We hope the following helps comprehend the scale at which LogHouse operates.
OpenTelemetry's efficiency challenges at extreme scale
#
Initially, we used OpenTelemetry (OTel) for all log collection. It was a great starting point and an established industry standard which allowed us to quickly establish a baseline where every pod in our Kubernetes environment shipped logs to ClickHouse.

data.title: Delta Chat is a decentralized and secure messenger app
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: Delta Chat是一款去中心化且安全的即时通讯应用，支持多账户和多设备，用户可选择使用安全快速的聊天邮件服务器或传统电子邮件服务器。它提供互动式网页应用，适用于游戏和协作，并经过审核的端到端加密，防止网络和服务器攻击。该软件是自由开源软件（FOSS），基于互联网标准构建，避免了xkcd927问题。支持移动和桌面设备，提供多语言版本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Delta Chat及其相关技术的优缺点，包括去中心化聊天工具的安全性、隐私性、可迁移性及其实现技术。

不同观点：
• **ZoomZoomZoom**：认为Delta Chat等去中心化工具虽然利用了现有基础设施，但依赖特定服务器，存在用户被切断服务器后难以迁移的问题。建议使用密钥对作为用户标识，以实现无缝的服务器切换，避免因国家审查导致账号失效。

• **heavyset_go**：指出Delta Chat基于IMAP和SMTP协议，虽然能保证消息内容的安全，但在隐私和匿名性方面表现不足。邮件系统本身并非为隐私设计，因此Delta Chat不适合用于身份和社交图谱的隐藏。

• **maqp**：强调Delta Chat缺乏完美前向安全性（PFS），如果私钥泄露，历史消息可能被解密。相比之下，Signal协议更为安全，因此不建议使用安全性较差的应用。

• **sixtiethutopia**：提到Delta Chat使用PGP加密，但不支持前向安全性，并且在收到未加密消息时会自动切换到未加密通信。还担心可能会受到降级攻击，即 adversaries 通过伪造发送地址使通信降级为未加密。

• **shark_laser**：推荐使用0xchat，它基于Nostr协议，支持私钥登录、加密聊天和闪电支付，具备去中心化和跨平台特性。

• **raybb**：关注用户在迁移到不同服务器时，是否能保持原有聊天记录，指出这是类似WhatsApp的痛点。

• **b0a04gl**：认为Delta Chat的优势在于利用现有IMAP和SMTP基础设施，避免了新服务器搭建和联盟管理问题，但挑战在于用户体验的提升。

补充讨论：
• **blancotech**：开玩笑地将Delta Chat与Delta航空公司混淆，表现出对其他类型聊天系统的兴趣。

• **fouronnes3**：关心作为小众聊天应用，Delta Chat如何应对垃圾信息防护问题，并提到Meta（如WhatsApp）的垃圾信息防护非常有效，可能与其要求手机号码注册有关。

• **lclc**：询问是否可以与Protonmail结合使用，并建议Protonmail可以基于此开发自己的聊天应用。

• **iqandjoke**：幽默地质疑开发者是否与CIA有关联，反映出对应用开发者背景的关注。

• **kingkawn**：简洁指出“相当好的保护”已不再足够，暗示需要更高标准的安全保护。

• **exe34**：讽刺地建议创建一个包括FBI和Shin Bet的群聊，表达了对安全和隐私的担忧。

• **seydor**：欣赏Delta Chat基于现有基础设施的去中心化设计，认为这是战争等极端情况下的可靠选择，并提出AI可能用于去中心化垃圾信息过滤。

争议焦点：
• Delta Chat依赖特定服务器的问题以及用户账号迁移的困难。
• Delta Chat在隐私和匿名性方面的不足，特别是基于非匿名设计的邮件系统。
• Delta Chat缺乏完美前向安全性，与Signal协议等更安全协议的比较。
• 去中心化应用如何有效防护垃圾信息的问题。

data.title: 'Gwada negative': French scientists find new blood type in woman
data.author: spidersouris
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新发现的血液类型及其影响

不同观点：
• [ajb] 认为原帖缺乏细节，并提供了法语文章链接以及国际输血协会（ISBT）的相关页面链接，指出ISBT已将新血液类型添加到他们的列表中，尽管页面显示仍为47种，但数据表中已更新。
• [kimos] 表示对血液类型数量的理解一直停留在约8种，发现有48种非常令人震惊。
• [kalium-xyz] 认为血液类型问题在大多数情况下不重要，但在某些情况下却至关重要。
• [tetris11] 对新血液类型被命名为PIGZ表示好奇。
• [escapecharacter] 调侃说，动漫粉丝维基可能会因此疯狂更新。

补充讨论：
• [thaumasiotes] 对新血液类型发现如何帮助解释某些病理现象表示疑问，特别是当三个兄弟姐妹因罕见血液类型而出现风湿病症状时，文章未详细说明他们是否定期接受输血。
• [xyst] 认为，尽管新发现令人兴奋，但对于患者来说，拥有罕见血液类型可能意味着更高的医疗成本和更复杂的治疗过程，尤其是在紧急情况下或远离常规医疗区域时，找到合适的医疗人员处理这种情况可能非常困难。

争议焦点：

**uBO Lite** (uBOL), an efficient [MV3 API-based](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/mv3/intro/) content blocker.
uBOL is entirely declarative, meaning there is no need for a permanent uBOL process for the filtering to occur, and CSS/JS injection-based content filtering is [performed reliably](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/scripting/#method-registerContentScripts) by the browser itself rather than by the extension. - uBlock Origin's built-in filter lists

data.title: Fundamental Problems of Lisp, the Cons Cell (2024)
data.author: gudzpoz
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了LISP语言中的一个基本问题：cons单元用于构建列表的局限性。LISP的核心是基于函数式编程和列表操作，但其列表结构依赖于硬件概念的cons单元，导致每个列表节点只能包含两个元素。若要构建更长的列表，必须嵌套cons单元并采用特殊解释方式，称为“适当列表”。这种设计限制了列表处理的发展，使得操作复杂且不统一。文章建议通过标准化适当列表和隐藏低级cons操作来改进LISP。同时，作者批评了cons及其相关函数（如car、cdr等）导致代码不一致和复杂性，并以假设语言gisp中的三元单元fons为例，说明了类似问题。最后，文章探讨了LISP的cons问题为何未被解决，归因于历史和技术限制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lisp中的cons细胞和其作为基础数据结构的角色

不同观点：
• noosphr认为Lisp的核心不是函数式编程，而是对抽象语法树的直接操作。同时，嵌套列表的深度通常较浅，复杂的操作很少见。Lisp的强大在于实现领域特定语言（DSL），如Emacs的elisp实现。
• lisper强调cons细胞作为原始数据结构的价值，指出其与C语言中指针操作的区别。认为cons细胞的问题在于不当的抽象使用，而非其本身有问题。
• DonaldFisk认为cons细胞是Lisp不可或缺的一部分，类似于Smalltalk中的对象和APL中的数组。其他语言也有类似的数据结构，Lisp程序员普遍认为cons细胞和列表非常有用。
• alphazard指出cons细胞的间接机制与其连接机制混淆的问题，建议将值的组合与存储分开处理，以实现更高效的内存使用。
• behnamoh提到Janet这个Lisp方言，虽然文档不足，但其编译成小二进制文件和支持图像的特点令人喜爱。
• gudzpoz分享了在为Lisp方言编写JIT运行时的经验，认为cons风格的链表在性能上难以与数组竞争，但正在尝试通过JIT优化来改进。
• smarks回顾了Xah Lee多年来对cons细胞的批评，认为这是一个老生常谈的问题，并引用了历史讨论中其他人的观点。
• Jtsummers通过引用LISP I手册，解释cons、car和cdr是用于创建和操作S表达式的原始工具，而非仅限于列表操作，强调其历史和合理性。
• dragontamer简要说明cons细胞作为基础数据结构的强大和灵活性，但也指出高性能现代编程中数组的重要性。
• chubot提到Clojure中cons细胞使用较少，因为其基于不可变的地图和向量。
• kazinator在TXR Lisp中展示了car/cdr的扩展使用，通过定义新结构和方法来实现更多功能。

补充讨论：
• 对Xah Lee的批评：多个评论者提到Xah Lee对cons细胞的批评，并对其观点提出质疑，认为其可能缺乏深入理解。
• 历史背景：smarks和Jtsummers都提到了Lisp的历史文档和早期讨论，提供了对cons细胞历史和设计的更深理解。
• 性能问题：gudzpoz和dragontamer都提到了cons细胞在现代硬件上的性能问题，并讨论了可能的优化方法。

争议焦点：
• cons细胞的抽象和使用是否恰当，以及其在现代编程需求下的性能和实用性。

44310996.article_content:
Fundamental Problems of LISP, the Cons Cell
By Xah Lee. Date:
2024-07-02
.
(this essay is originally written around 2008)
The Cons Business
The other fundamental problem in the language is its cons cells as its list construction primitive.
Lisp at core is based on functional programing on lists.
This is a powerful paradigm.
However, for historical reasons, lisp's list is based on the hardware concept of âconsâ cell.
From a mathematical, functional, API point of view, what this means is that lisp's âlistâ is limited to a max of 2 elements.
If you want a longer list, you must nest it and interpret it in a special way.
(i.e.
effectively creating a mini-protocol, known as âproper listâ.)
The cons fundamentally crippled the development of list processing.
Lisp being historically based the cons for about 4 decades. The cons and the associated {car cdr cadr caadr caddr caaar cdddr â¦} are fundamentally rooted in the lisp langs, is thus not something that can be easily mended. This is unfortunate. However, this situation could be improved.  By, for example:
Create a standard that all list data structures must be proper lists. (this would also mean re-implement association lists to be based on proper lists)
Expose only higher-level list manipulation functions (i.e. interfaces to cons) in all new literature.
Even mark cons related constructs as obsolete.
One of the myth that is quickly injected into budding lispers, is that cons is powerful. It is powerful in the sense assembly lang is powerful.
Lisp's cons is perhaps the greatest fuck up in the history of computer languages.
Racket Lisp described the cons problem well:
Racket Doc on Lisp Cons Problem
For some concrete examples of problems caused by the cons, see:
Guy Steele Says: Don't Iterate, Recurse, and Get rid of lisp cons!
Why Lisp Not Have a Generic Copy-List Function?
Lisp List Problem
Frequently Asked Questions
If you don't like cons, lisp has arrays and hashmaps, too.
Suppose there's a lang called gisp.
In gisp, there's cons but also fons.
Fons is just like cons except it has 3 cells with 3 accessors: car, cbr, cdr.
Now, gisp is a old lang, the fons are deeply rooted in the lang.
Every some 100 lines of code you'll see a use of fons with its extra accessor cbr, or any one of the cbaar, cdabr, cbbar, cbbbar, etc.
You got annoyed by this.
You complain that fons is bad.
But then some gisp fanatics retorts: âIf you don't like fons, gisp has cons, too!â.
You see, by âhaving something tooâ, does not solve the problem of pollution.
I like the cons concept. Even in functional languages like Haskell it is popular, for example, when matching in the form of (x:xs), which is the same like car/cdr in Lisp.
Languages that have a list data type implemented as linked list, with First, Rest accessors, do not expose it as API in the same way lisp does with explicit cons.
Lisp's cons forces programer to think of list in a low-level nested of 2-item construction, with explicit functions like âcddrâ, âcadaarâ etc, and even a special notation â(A .
B)â.
This hinders the development tree functions.
For example, one might write a function that extracts the leafs of a binary tree.
But due to cons, there is no single data structure to implement a binary tree.
You can have the whole structure made of cons, or cons only for ending branches, or whole structure made of âproper listâ.
Consequently, what's considered a leaf depends on your implementation, and the code to traverse the tree also depends on how you used cons.
Worse, any proper list can have improper list as elements.
So, you can have a list of cons, or cons of lists, cons of cons, list of lists, or any mix.
The overall effect of the cons is that it prevents lisp to have a uniform high level treatment of lists, with the result that development of functions that work on tree are inconsistent and few.
2009-07-21 Addendum : there was actually a lang with âfonsâ of 3 cells. {Haines, E.
C., The TREET List Processing Language.
M.S.
Thesis, MIT, Cambridge, Mass., August 1964.
Also SR-133, The MITRE Corporation, Bedford, Mass., April 1965.} Thanks to
Richard Fateman
for alerting me to this.
Why Lisp's Cons Problem Never Got Fixed?
Now, a little speculation.
We might wonder, why lisp has the cons problem and was never addressed in Common Lisp or Scheme Lisp?
Historical Necessity
I guess at the time, 1960s and 1970s, the very fact that you could have a concept like a list in a lang and manipulate it as a unit, is a very advanced concept.
The list, being built up by hardware cons, is just something that is necessary for implementation for practical considerations.
(think for a moment what computers are like in the 1960s.)
Having data as a single manipulable object (list) didn't really become popular until the 1990s.
(notably due to Perl) And today, it is THE most important feature of high-level languages.
(e.g. Perl Python Ruby PHP JavaScript)
Deep Nesting is Rare
The lisp's cons, as a underlyin

• lisper强调cons细胞作为原始数据结构的价值，指出其与C语言中指针操作的区别。认为cons细胞的问题在于不当的抽象使用，而非其本身有问题。
• DonaldFisk认为cons细胞是Lisp不可或缺的一部分，类似于Smalltalk中的对象和APL中的数组。其他语言也有类似的数据结构，Lisp程序员普遍认为cons细胞和列表非常有用。
• alphazard指出cons细胞的间接机制与其连接机制混淆的问题，建议将值的组合与存储分开处理，以实现更高效的内存使用。
• behnamoh提到Janet这个Lisp方言，虽然文档不足，但其编译成小二进制文件和支持图像的特点令人喜爱。
• gudzpoz分享了在为Lisp方言编写JIT运行时的经验，认为cons风格的链表在性能上难以与数组竞争，但正在尝试通过JIT优化来改进。
• smarks回顾了Xah Lee多年来对cons细胞的批评，认为这是一个老生常谈的问题，并引用了历史讨论中其他人的观点。
• Jtsummers通过引用LISP I手册，解释cons、car和cdr是用于创建和操作S表达式的原始工具，而非仅限于列表操作，强调其历史和合理性。
• dragontamer简要说明cons细胞作为基础数据结构的强大和灵活性，但也指出高性能现代编程中数组的重要性。
• chubot提到Clojure中cons细胞使用较少，因为其基于不可变的地图和向量。
• kazinator在TXR Lisp中展示了car/cdr的扩展使用，通过定义新结构和方法来实现更多功能。

补充讨论：
• 对Xah Lee的批评：多个评论者提到Xah Lee对cons细胞的批评，并对其观点提出质疑，认为其可能缺乏深入理解。
• 历史背景：smarks和Jtsummers都提到了Lisp的历史文档和早期讨论，提供了对cons细胞历史和设计的更深理解。
• 性能问题：gudzpoz和dragontamer都提到了cons细胞在现代硬件上的性能问题，并讨论了可能的优化方法。

争议焦点：
• cons细胞的抽象和使用是否恰当，以及其在现代编程需求下的性能和实用性。

data.author: neural_thing
data.article_summary: 《MMOndrian Rectangles》是由Sergey Alexashenko创作的一款在线互动艺术工具。用户可以通过点击和拖动等操作，对画面进行重新着色、添加或删除线条以及移动和缩放视图。左键点击用于重新着色，右键点击用于添加或删除线条，拖动用于移动线条或平移画面，滚动则用于缩放。该工具提供了简便的交互方式，让用户在抽象几何图形中进行艺术创作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对某互动应用程序的使用体验和功能反馈

不同观点：
• gschizas：用户无法正常使用该应用，点击没有任何效果，控制台没有错误信息，但能看到一些网络流量（如WSS、XHR）。唯一的反馈是右键点击时显示坐标信息。
• pimlottc：误以为该应用与 Ultima 游戏有关，提到了 Mondain。
• juancroldan：对应用的概念表示喜爱，并好奇是先有应用创意还是文字游戏（双关语）。
• detourdog：询问应用是否使用了DeStijl宣言中的规则来使用颜色和线条。
• ggrelet：怀疑网站是否已经失效。
• Heliodex：对应用给予积极评价，分享了领土占领策略，如选择颜色、占领区域和细分区域等。
• sublinear：到达应用时发现已经被过度细分，有人用颜色写出了“ASS”。
• brulard：编辑的内容很快消失，或者只能维持20秒左右。
• graypegg：收到“连接过多”的错误信息，并表示由于频繁点击感到抱歉。
• dmwood：喜欢该应用，但希望能保存图像为SVG格式，而不仅仅是截图。
• dunham：无法平移，且缩放不会缩放到鼠标位置，但成功写出了"HI"。
• leoff：觉得合并方块最有趣，但遇到服务器拒绝合并的bug。
• thunkingdeep：应用无法正常工作，点击的内容会自动取消。
• remram：删除线条功能不正常，线条会短暂消失然后重新出现。

补充讨论：
• 用户对应用的功能（如平移、缩放、合并方块、删除线条等）存在较多抱怨和bug反馈。
• 有用户对应用的创意表示喜爱，但也对其实现和功能提出了改进建议。
• 服务器负载问题（如连接过多）导致部分用户无法正常使用应用。
• 应用的互动性和策略性（如领土占领、细分区域等）得到了部分用户的积极评价。

data.author: tkhattra

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lua语言中数组和表的设计以及性能优化问题

不同观点：
• [nzzn] 认为Lua使用表（table）类型来同时表示字典和数组，虽然保持了语言的简洁性，但数组在实际应用中非常常见，其他同类动态语言普遍支持数组类型。他认为数组应该成为Lua的核心语言特性，尽管对新手来说可能增加一些学习成本，但长远来看是值得的。

• [ufo] 提到数组优化的可能方案，特别是"Reflected Arrays"版本，并暗示这一优化可能会出现在Lua的下一个版本中，提供了相关链接以供参考。

• [marhee] 质疑Lua程序中是否真的经常使用具有相同类型的大型连续数组，并建议可以通过标记和单类型标签来优化这种情况，认为这样可以简单有效地优化内存使用，满足98%的使用场景。

• [Jyaif] 强烈批评Lua当前数组设计中的内存浪费问题，指出可以通过使用`__attribute__((packed))`来解决问题，并指责Lua没有在配置文件`luaconf.h`中宣传这一选项是不负责任的。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Lua数组设计的简洁性与性能优化之间的平衡。一部分人认为Lua应保持简单，而另一部分人则认为应针对特定场景（如大型同类型数组）进行优化以提升性能。
• 讨论还涉及到具体的优化方案，如通过特定语法或编译选项（如`__attribute__((packed))`）来减少内存浪费。
• 时间点的提及（[kzrdude]）指出相关讨论是基于2024年9月的一个较新的发布版本，表明这是一个相对较新的问题。

data.title: ARIA, the UK's Bet to Build Scientific Revolutions
data.author: almost-exactly
data.article_summary: 《ARIA：英国构建科学革命的尝试》一文介绍了英国高级研究与发明局（ARIA）的使命与运作模式。ARIA常被称为“英国的DARPA”，但并非简单复制，而是受DARPA启发，如采用任期有限的项目主管来领导和管理外部研究团队。ARIA的目标是通过支持大胆、非共识的科学创意，催生重大技术突破，改变人们对可能性的认知。与DARPA不同，ARIA在设立时经过精心设计，确保其独立性和自主性，避免过多政治干预。ARIA与风投公司不同，它更关注高风险、高回报的“可能实现的重大突破”，旨在推动经济、生活质量和全球科技进步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国新成立的政府资助尖端研究机构（ARIA）的潜在影响和挑战

不同观点：
• [AnotherGoodName] 认为成立这样的研究机构是理所当然的，并以澳大利亚的CSIRO为例，指出其历史成就和经济回报，如WiFi技术和选择性育种，表明政府资助的研究所能带来巨大收益。

• [nickdothutton] 对ARIA的前景持怀疑态度，认为政府对研发的关注短暂且不稳定，监管障碍是主要问题。以英国在核能研究领域的落后为例，说明英国在多个研究领域面临类似问题。

• [hdivider] 支持ARIA的成立，但希望英国能引入类似美国SBIR/STTR的计划，尤其要避免只惠及精英机构如牛津和剑桥，强调小企业的重要性及其在创新中的巨大影响。

• [ggm] 回顾了英国过去如NPL和Daresbury等研究机构的成就与失败，指出成功的研发需要接受可能的巨大失败，并以DARPA为例，说明持续资金支持的重要性。

• [alun] 肯定ARIA的成立是一个积极步骤，但强调其成功取决于是否能避免短期主义，选择无私且有远见的领导者，以应对长期研究项目。

• [simianwords] 关注ARIA的运作模式，质疑其市场激励机制，尤其是是否像风投公司那样通过股权换取资金支持。

补充讨论：
• ARIA的成功与否可能取决于其能否克服政府短期主义和监管障碍。
• 不同评论者对政府资助研究机构的历史成就和未来潜力有不同看法，部分乐观，部分持怀疑态度。
• 强调领导层选择和机构文化对于长期研究项目的重要性。
• 对ARIA具体运作模式和市场激励机制的关注，提出了是否采用类似风险投资模式的疑问。

The UK’s Advanced Research and Invention Agency (ARIA) is often referred to as a “UK DARPA”. While ARIA is no DARPA clone, many features of the agency are admittedly DARPA-inspired, such as the use of term-limited program managers, which ARIA calls program directors. These program directors serve as chief visionaries for their programs as well as fund and actively manage teams of coordinated external researchers towards a program's well-defined goal. Despite these similarities, the founding team at ARIA views their work as a metascience experiment all its own. ARIA’s ultimate aim is to drive economic output, quality of life improvements, health benefits, and innovation in the UK. The strengths, needs, and context of the modern UK R&D ecosystem shape the agency’s structure at least as much as lessons from DARPA history.
Any given ARIA program is meant to catalyze progress towards big-if-true, non-consensus ideas. These programs each represent different bets that fall within what ARIA calls ‘opportunity spaces.’ Opportunity spaces delineate areas that ARIA and its program managers believe might be ideal places to create big-if-true technology waves.The expectation is not that each program achieves positive results, but instead materially “changes the conversation” regarding what’s possible in a space.
To better understand the ARIA experiment, Eric Gilliam, author of the
FreakTakes blog
and expert on the history of R&D organizations, sat down for a three-hour interview with Ilan Gur, CEO of ARIA. Prior to joining ARIA as its first CEO, Ilan was a founding program manager at ARPA-E, the founder of a lithium battery startup, founding director of Cyclotron Road, and founder of Activate. At ARPA-E, Ilan took a special interest in finding better ways to commercialize exciting research. At Activate and Cyclotron Road, he built fellowships that served as perches for researchers working on societally important ‘ hard’ technologies that might not yet be VC-fundable find their feet and begin developing technologies into market-ready products.
This interview was edited for brevity and clarity, but the full transcript and video can be found at
FreakTakes
.

Eric Gilliam:
ARIA is called a “UK DARPA,” but it’s different in many ways. How is ARIA similar to DARPA, and how is it different?
Ilan Gur:
When ARIA was created, the tagline was, “A DARPA for the UK.” But we were not set up to be a DARPA. DARPA was created in the United States 70 years ago. How that model translates to the UK is not obvious. However, if you want an existence proof of a funding agency doing things differently and having massively transformative outcomes, DARPA is that existence proof.
In setting up ARIA, the U.K. government also went through a very deliberate process to make sure that it had independence and freedoms to be able to do all of the best things that early DARPA was able to do. And I think it's worth calling out that Parliament, civil servants, and others involved in this got this right. There’s not a ton of political intervention. The processes that do exist are reasonable and make sure we’re responsible stewards of taxpayer funds. But they also weren't prescriptive in what ARIA looks like. We have the freedom to build the agency from first principles.
I sometimes say that the UK government set up a “stem cell of an R&D funding agency,” and now we're trying to differentiate it towards something that changes the world.
Fundamentally, we're meant to take bold bets that amplify different parts of the research system in new ways. I think about our programs as funding a constellation of teams that can lead to massively transformative outcomes at the intersection of quality of life and economic growth — not just for the UK, but for the world. That “for the world” bit is really about the scale of ambition that we are talking about.
E:
How are ARIA’s ambitions different from, say, a deep tech venture capital firm’s?
I:
While some VCs are just in it to make money, a lot of VCs see venture capital as a platform to change the trajectory of the future in positive ways. We share that vision. But the big difference between ARIA and VC is twofold. When thinking about the bar of “big-if-true,” it's important to think about both the sense of scale — “how big is ‘big’?” — and how speculative you are willing to get on the “if-true?”

• [simianwords] 关注ARIA的运作模式，质疑其市场激励机制，尤其是是否像风投公司那样通过股权换取资金支持。

• 强调领导层选择和机构文化对于长期研究项目的重要性。
• 对ARIA具体运作模式和市场激励机制的关注，提出了是否采用类似风险投资模式的疑问。

data.title: Denmark's Archaeology Experiment Is Paying Off in Gold and Knowledge
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 丹麦通过允许业余金属探测爱好者上交文物，推动了一项激进的考古实验，取得了丰硕成果。自2020年以来，探测者Ole Ginnerup Schytz在丹麦农田中发现了大量金质圆盘，其中一枚刻有“他是奥丁的人”的护身符（bracteate），将奥丁崇拜的历史提前了150年。这些发现揭示了丹麦过去的面貌，包括庙宇、贸易路线和定居点。丹麦鼓励公众参与金属探测，并与政府考古学家合作，每年上交超过2万件物品，远超邻国的考古成果。这项计划使丹麦在考古研究上领先于其他欧洲国家。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：金属探测、文物发现及其相关问题

不同观点：
• [comrade1234] 分享了个人在瑞士一片古森林中每年采蘑菇的经历，并提到发现古代陶锅残片及潜在的洞穴。虽然对使用金属探测器寻找宝藏感兴趣，但因当地法律限制而作罢。他认为罗马人在瑞士活动频繁，但未必在他提到的区域。

• [BurningFrog] 对人们上交维京时代金 artifacts 的行为表示赞赏，并建议应根据金属价值给予奖励，以减少将文物私自保留的诱惑。他认为这样可以避免有价值的发现流失。

• [erk__] 提到丹麦的Danefæ和Danekræ收藏，前者为人造文物，后者为非人造重要物品。Danekræ收藏数量较少，目前仅1054件，且可在网上查看，但生物标本和地质标本未包括在内。

• [biophysboy] 推荐丹麦靠近Kronborg城堡的海事博物馆，馆内有数百件模型船、沉船 artifacts 和高质量的水下照片，建议游览哥本哈根时参观。

• [roger_] 提问探测者上交文物后是否会获得某种证书以表彰其诚实。

• [trhway] 提出使用无人机或自主遥控车悬挂金属探测器的想法，认为在乌克兰大规模排雷后，这种技术可能应用于考古等领域。

• [thaumasiotes] 对Ginnerup发现的带有Odin铭文的bracteate提出不同看法，认为虽然该发现将Odin崇拜历史延长了150年，但罗马人早在几个世纪前就已记录了日耳曼神祇，并使用“Mercury”来指代Odin，这表明神祇本质未变。

补充讨论：
• [countrymile] 提到了一部名为《Detectorists》的英国喜剧，认为它对金属探测工作有独特的英式视角，并推荐给感兴趣的人。

• [wewewedxfgdf] 提到一个带有纳粹符号的文物，但指出该符号早在纳粹采用前1500年就已存在，澄清了符号的历史背景。

争议焦点：
• [thaumasiotes] 对Ginnerup发现的历史解释提出质疑，认为尽管发现重要，但对Odin崇拜历史的解读可能存在误差，尤其是对罗马文献的解读存在不同看法。

整体讨论围绕文物发现、金属探测的合法性、技术应用及历史解释展开，各方提供了个人经验、建议和学术观点。

Denmark’s Radical Archaeology Experiment Is Paying Off in Gold and Knowledge
The Danish government deputized private detectorists to unearth artifacts buried in farm fields. Their finds are revealing the country’s past in extraordinary detail
By
Elizabeth Anne Brown
edited by
Kate Wong
Kristen Nedergaard Dreiøe (
left
) and Marie Aagaard Larsen (
right
) swing their metal detectors over a field where grain is typically grown in southern Denmark.
Alastair Philip Wiper
O
le Ginnerup Schytz, an engineer in Denmark’s sleepy Vindelev agricultural area, had used a metal detector only a handful of times when he found a bent clump of metal in a friend’s barley field. He figured it was the lid from a container of tinned fish and tossed it in his junk bag with the other bits of farm trash that had set his metal detector beeping: rusty nails, screws, scrap iron. A few paces away he dug up another shiny circle. Someone had clearly enjoyed a lot of tinned fish here—into the sack it went. But when Ginnerup found a
third
metal round, he stopped to take a closer look. Wiping the mud from its surface, he suddenly found himself face-to-face with a Roman emperor. At that point he had to admit “they weren’t food cans,” Ginnerup recalls with a chuckle.
After a brief intermission for an online Teams meeting for work that December day in 2020, Ginnerup dug up 14
glittering gold disks—some as big as saucers—that archaeologists say were buried about 1,500 years ago, during a time of chaos after ash clouds from a distant volcanic eruption created a miniature ice age. Four medallions feature Roman emperors, and several bear intricate geometric patterns. But the real showstopper is an amulet called a bracteate with two stylized designs: a man in profile, his long hair pulled back in a braid, and a horse in full gallop. An expert in ancient runes says she was awestruck when she finally made out the inscription on top: “He is Odin’s man.”
These embossed runes are the oldest known written mention of Odin, the Norse god of war and ruler of Valhalla. Ginnerup’s bracteate, which archaeologists describe as the most significant Danish find in centuries, extended the worship of Odin back 150 years—and it’s all because Ginnerup received a metal detector as a birthday present from his father-in-law.
On supporting science journalism
If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by
subscribing
. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
Many other European countries have prohibited or heavily restricted hobbyist metal detecting, but Denmark has embraced it, creating a system for members of the public to hand over finds to government archaeologists. The result has been an embarrassment of riches, with more than 20,000 items turned in annually in recent years. The curators assigned to identify and catalog the artifacts can’t dream of keeping up, but the fruits of their collective labor are clear: whereas neighboring countries have only vague sketches of the past, metal detectorists have filled in the ancient map of Denmark with temple complexes, trade routes and settlements that would have otherwise been lost to history.
“Private detectorists have rocketed Denmark ahead of its neighbors in archaeological research,” says Torben Trier Christiansen, curator of archaeology at Denmark’s North Jutland Museums. “There’s nothing ‘amateur’ about them.”
Denmark has been inhabited since the end of the last ice age, when nomadic hunter-gatherers from southern Europe arrived following the migration of reindeer and retreating glaciers as early as 12,500 years ago. The ancestors of modern ethnic Danes showed up some 5,000 years ago, journeying from the steppes of what is now Ukraine and southwestern Russia. Their descendants lived in small farming communities across Scandinavia for thousands of years, building megaliths and barrows for their honored dead and making human sacrifices in bogs to appease their gods.
In the early centuries of the common era, these farming communities coalesced into a series of Germanic tribes—the Cimbri, the Teutons, the Jutes, the Angles and the Danes—who became skilled seafarers, explorers and metalworkers. Because precious metals—including silver, gold and the components of bronze—do not occur naturally in what is now Denmark, its denizens had to barter for or steal these metals from abroad. They traded extensively with the Roman Empire, which never reached as far north as Scandinavia.
Detectorist Ole Ginnerup Schytz found this gold amulet, or bracteate, bearing the inscription "He is Odin's man." The find extends the worship of Odin back 150 years. (The swastika design next to the man's head predates the adoption of this symbol by the Nazis.)
Arnold Mikkelsen/National Museum of Denmark

data.title: Balatro for the Nintendo E-Reader
data.author: arantius
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了将2024年最佳游戏候选者《Balatro》移植到一个古老且 obscure 的平台——任天堂E-Reader上的可能性。作者热爱《Balatro》，这是一款结合了扑克和纸牌的单人游戏。作者尝试制作了一个E-Reader上的原型，虽然部分界面和功能是模拟的，但核心游戏玩法已经实现。由于E-Reader的技术限制，如屏幕分辨率和显示数字的限制，完整移植存在挑战，尤其是处理高分和大量不同的Joker卡牌。此外，E-Reader的存储空间有限，无法容纳《Balatro》所有的150张Joker卡牌和大量文本。尽管如此，作者认为通过适当简化和重新设计，仍可能创造出一款保留游戏精髓的简化版。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Balatro游戏的技术实现、游戏体验及其相关争议

不同观点：
• Waterluvian认为32位与64位对得分影响不大，因为Balatro的得分远超uint64的最大值，推测使用了某种数值抽象类型。
• Sram1337建议将分数编码为实际值的10倍，例如将1.5编码为15，从而减少最大得分并解决小数问题，同时需要放弃0.01的卡片。
• Im3w1l认为浮点数是可行的，因为Balatro并不需要每秒进行数十亿次的浮点运算。
• Anyfoo表示不理解Balatro的吸引力，认为其过于简化，几乎是“数字上升”游戏，类似于Cookie Clicker，但Balatro有更多的游戏元素，尽管如此，这种直接的“数字上升”让他感到不太喜欢。

补充讨论：
• Azhenley提到作者曾开发E-Reader上的射击游戏，并表示希望看到更多类似的互联网内容。
• Nate75Sanders分享了Balatro在Commodore 64上的版本链接，称赞其在平台限制下的出色表现。
• Kinduff对Playstack和LocalThunk下架此类移植作品表示遗憾，认为这只会让游戏社区更加壮大。
• Fisherjeff对作者表示同情，庆幸自己早先摆脱了对Balatro的沉迷。
• Dwedit讨论了在遇到精灵限制问题时的解决方案，建议对静止物体使用背景层，而不是占用精灵槽，并提出可以通过使用重叠层实现不同的对齐方式。

争议焦点：
• Balatro的简化游戏机制及其“数字上升”的核心玩法引起了部分玩家的不满（anyfoo的观点），而另一部分玩家（如EA-3167和Nate75Sanders）则高度赞赏其在技术限制下的出色表现和游戏的独特魅力。

44339025.article_content:
What if the best game of 2024 came out on an old, obscure and weird platform?
I friggin'
love
Balatro. I've put an embarrassing number of hours into it. I also like to make games for the Nintendo E-Reader. The E-Reader was a peripheral for the Game Boy Advance that let you load mini games and "DLC" by scanning cards into it.
The E-Reader attached to a Game Boy Advance (image by Nintendo)
Oh and Balatro is a single player solitaire/poker hybrid game that is super fun. If you enjoy poker, solitaire, or especially trading card games like Magic the Gathering or Pokemon, you should definitely check it out if you haven't already.
A while back, I made this mock up screenshot of what Balatro might look like on the
E-Reader.
A mock up of Balatro on the E-Reader
This mock up was really fun to make. So I decided to take it one step further and make a working prototype of the game. This was also a blast to make!
This prototype is
almost
entirely real. It's a real E-Reader game, and it really plays Balatro. I only implemented just what you see in the video, so it's a very long way away from being a full port of the game.
I said it's almost entirely real because it does fake a few things. The blind selection screen is entirely a mock. You just press A and go into the round.
The blind selection screen is completely mocked
And when you win the round, the win screen is mocked too. You have to win with two remaining hands for it to be believable :)
The blind selection screen is completely mocked
But playing the game within the round is 99% real. I hard coded Fibonacci and Splash jokers, and when it calculates what type of hand was played, it only knows about "duplicative" style hands (ie two pair, full house, three of a kind, etc). My wife was sad to find her straight only got scored as a high card. Doh. Many other things are missing too, but this was mostly due to not wanting to spend too much time on this project more than anything.
Could it be done?
Would it be possible to make Balatro for the E-Reader? I think so.
It would be a challenging project and a good number of concessions would need to be made. But I do think a demaked version that still captures the essence and fun of the game is doable.
Dealing with high scores
An immediate challenge would be the massive scores you can get in Balatro. E-Reader games can comfortably work with 32 bit numbers. So the highest possible score would be 4,294,967,295. Real Balatro uses 64 bit numbers so scores can absolutely go into the stratosphere there. But I think 4 billion is still plenty to have fun and get that Balatro experience.
There's more bad news here. We'll talk about it below in the small numbers section.
But ... the Game Boy Advance's screen is only 240x160 pixels, so fitting such large numbers onto the screen would be a challenge. This is an area the demake would have to be different from the real thing. Something like this would be needed (just a quick mock up).
A UI change to accomodate larger scores
So many numbers
Balatro puts a lot of numbers on the screen.
Number of remaining hands
Number of remaining discards
Current ante
Current round
How many cards remain in the deck
How large the deck is
The level of the hand that is being played
The current chip total
The current mult total
Your money
Your score so far in the round
Your score for the current hand
The goal score to beat the round
Did I miss any? The E-Reader has a collection of
DrawNumber
functions, but the problem is it is limited to four unique numbers. If you try to draw a fifth number with
DrawNumber
, nothing happens.
Even worse, each number can have a max of 5 digits. So just to keep track of your score, would take up 2 of those number slots.
A lot of this can be worked around with sprites and some clever redesigning and careful pruning back of features (this would be a demake after all). I do think this challenge could be overcome, but it would probably be the hardest part of this project.
150 jokers?
Balatro has 150 jokers, and they all do very different things. I think making a full fledged "joker engine" that can handle this is doable. The E-Reader/GBA has plenty of memory for this, and it's easy to dynamically call functions. So logic-wise, I don't think this would be a problem. But each joker needs a card graphic.
Five Joker cards in the demaked style
That would really add up and take up a ton of space. Space is always a concern with E-Reader games. Make no doubt, Balatro on the E-Reader would be a very large game by E-Reader standards. But I'm certain fitting all 150 jokers would not be possible. A careful sub-selection of jokers would need to be picked.
Text
Balatro has a ton of text in it. Similar to games like Magic the Gathering, the rules of the game are literally written out on the cards. Balatro uses little text pop outs for this, but it's still the same idea.
The Wee Joker showing its rules pop up
There would be no way to include all this text into an E-Reader demake. So unfortunately the

威廉·普莱费尔（William Playfair, 1759-1823）是一位集间谍、无赖和学者于一身的复杂人物，他参与了18世纪和19世纪许多重大历史事件，常以不道德的角色出现。他发明了条形图和饼图，并 pioneer 使用了折线图。普莱费尔出生于苏格兰，早年为蒸汽机发明者詹姆斯·瓦特工作，后在伦敦经商失败并卷入欺诈。他参与了巴黎的法国大革命，并在革命期间从事交易，后因恐怖统治逃离法国。

普莱费尔参与了美国Scioto公司的土地骗局，欺骗法国贵族和乔治·华盛顿，最终美国政府不得不介入。他还在伦敦创办银行，再次因欺诈指控失败。债务缠身的普莱费尔被关入监狱，期间继续写作，包括其著名的数据可视化作品。他曾为英国政府从事间谍活动，窃取法国信号系统情报，并策划通过伪造纸币引发法国通货膨胀。晚年试图敲诈苏格兰贵族未果，最终破产。

普莱费尔在其1786年著作《商业与政治图集》中发明了条形图，并在《统计摘要》中进一步发展了数据可视化方法。他的创新对现代图表设计产生了深远影响。

44309734.article_content:
A spy, a scoundrel, and a scholar
William Playfair was all three. He led an extraordinary life at the heart of many of the great events of the 18th and 19th centuries, mostly in morally dubious roles. Among all the intrigue, scandal, and indebtedness, he found time to invent the bar and pie charts, and make pioneering use of line charts. As we'll see, he was quite a character.
Playfair the scoundrel
Playfair's lifetime (1759-1823) contained some momentous events:
The development of the steam engine
The French revolution
American independence and the establishment of a new US government
The introduction of paper money
and in different ways, some of them fraudulent, Playfair played a role.
He was born in 1759 in Dundee, Scotland, and due to his father's death, he was apprenticed to the inventor of the threshing machine at age 13. From there, he went to work for one of the leading producers of steam engines, James Watt. So far, this is standard "pull yourself up by your bootstraps with family connections" stuff. Things started to go awry when he moved to London in 1782 where he set up a silversmith company and was granted several patents. The business failed with some hints of impropriety, which was a taste of things to come.
In 1787, he moved to Paris where he sold steam engines and was a dealmaking middleman. This meant he knew the leading figures of French society. He was present at the storming of the Bastille in 1789 and may have had some mid-level command role there. During the revolution, he continued to do deals and work with the French elite, but he made enemies along the way. As the reign of terror got going, Playfair fled the country.
Before fleeing, Playfair had a hand in the Scioto Company, a company formed to sell land to settlers in the Ohio Valley in the new United States. The idea of setting up in a new land was of course attractive to the French elite who could see how the revolution was going.  The trouble was, the land was in territory controlled by Native Americans and it was also undeveloped and remote. In other words, completely unsuited for the French Bourgeoisie who were buying the land for a fresh start. The scheme even ended up entangling George Washington. It all ended badly and the US government had to step in to clean up the mess. This is considered to be the first major scandal in US history.
By 1793, Playfair was back in London where he helped formed a security bank, similar to institutions he'd been involved with in France.  Of course, it failed with allegations of fraud.
Playfair had always been a good writer and good at explaining data. He'd produced several books and pamphlets, and by the mid-1790s, he was trying to earn a living at it. But things didn't go too well, and he ended up imprisoned for debt in the notorious Fleet Prison (released in 1802). He tried to write his way out of debt, and notably, some of his most influential books were written while in prison.
There were no official government spying agencies at the time, but the British government quite happily paid for freelancers to do it, which may be an early example of "plausible deniability". Playfair was one such freelance secret agent. He discovered the secrets of the breakthrough French semaphore system while living in Frankfurt and handed them over to the British government in the mid-1790s. He was also the mastermind behind an audacious scheme to bring down the French government through massive counterfeiting and inflation.  The idea was simple, counterfeit French "paper money" and flood the country with high-quality fakes, stoking inflation and bringing down the currency and hence the government. The scheme may have worked as the currency collapsed and Napoleon took power in a coup in 1799, though Napoleon was worse for the British government than what had existed before.
By 1816, Playfair was broke
again
. What better way to get money quickly than a spot of blackmail targeted against Lord Archibald Douglas, the wealthiest man in Scotland? If you can dispute his parentage (and therefore his rights to his fortune), you can make a killing. Like many of Playfair's other schemes, this one failed too.
Bar charts and pie charts
Playfair invented the bar chart in his 1786 book, "Commercial and Political Atlas". He wanted to show Scottish imports and exports but didn't have enough data for a time series plot. All he had was imports and exports from different countries and he wanted to display the information in a way that would help his book sell. Here it is, the first bar chart. It shows imports and exports to and from Scotland by country.
This was such a new concept that Playfair had to provide instructions on how to read it.

data.title: P-Hacking in Startups
data.author: thaisstein
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了初创企业在敏捷实验中可能陷入的p-hacking陷阱，特别是在快速交付的压力下，团队容易报告任何看似改进的结果。文章通过三个案例说明了p-hacking的问题及如何避免：

1. **多重比较未修正**：在A/B/n测试中，同时测试多个版本增加了假阳性概率。应使用Bonferroni修正，调整显著性阈值以减少错误。

2. **结果出来后重新定义指标**：在未发现显著改进后，转而分析其他指标（如用户留存率），可能导致随机性错误。预先注册分析计划可避免这种问题。

3. **数据窥视**：频繁查看实验结果并根据其调整实验设计，会增加假阳性风险。应在实验开始前设定明确的分析计划和查看次数。

通过这些措施，团队可以提高实验结果的可靠性，避免因p-hacking做出错误决策。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：A/B测试和实验设计在初创公司中的应用及所需的严谨性

不同观点：
• Jemaclus认为，对于大多数初创公司来说，A/B测试不需要像医学研究那样严谨。除非公司的目标是追求统计显著性，否则在软件开发中，错误是可以修正的，不需要过度严谨。
• mo_42指出，在某些情况下，A/B测试可能不是最合适的方法，建议考虑用户体验研究方法，尤其是在当前样本量或测试设置难以检测到变化的情况下。
• simonw认为，在未达到产品市场契合之前，进行这类严谨的测试是浪费时间，建议先构建功能并观察用户使用情况。
• kdamica强烈反对过度严谨，认为初创公司实验的错误成本很低，建议进行大量实验，接受一些错误的积极结果，而不是将其视为绝对真理。
• ec109685强调频繁进行A/B测试会消耗统计“信用”，建议采用一些方法如季度alpha账本、Benjamini–Hochberg (BH)方法和Bayesian shrinkage + 5% "ghost"控制来减少误差。
• dooglius建议使用多臂赌博机方法来代替统计显著性测试，特别是在公司目标是优化页面以获取最大利润的情况下。
• kylecazar补充说，如果用户数量不足，应依赖直觉和关注核心产品，而不是进行这些测试。
• psychoslave请求推荐在线资源以学习P值相关知识。
• tmoertel指出文章中的一些百分号缺失可能导致 confusion。
• andy99质疑优化网站仪表盘增加用户注册是否是早期初创公司的核心行为。
• cornel_io认为，大多数初创公司无法像大公司那样收集大量数据，因此需要快速做出决策，建议采用更实际的策略，接受一些错误的积极结果以推动产品改进。
• ryan-duve表示，在选择UI布局时，不需要通过p值阈值，只需根据点估计选择成本相同且注册最多的布局。
• hlieberman建议使用多臂赌博机优化方法如epsilon-greedy算法。
• esafak推荐Spotify的博客以获取更多相关信息。
• NoahZuniga对第一个图中的p值为什么不总和为1提出疑问。

补充讨论：
• 不同观点主要集中在A/B测试的严谨性、替代方法和实际操作中的策略选择。
• 一些评论关注具体的技术细节如Bonferroni修正、多臂赌博机方法和Bayesian shrinkage等，以减少实验中的误差。
• 争议的焦点在于初创公司是否需要像医学研究一样严谨地进行A/B测试，以及如何在快速变化的环境中有效地进行实验设计和决策。

Speed kills rigor. In startups, the pressure to ship fast pushes teams to report
anything
that looks like an improvement. Thatâs how p-hacking happens. This piece breaks down three common casesâand how to avoid them.
Example 01: Multiple comparisons without correction
Imagine you're a product manager trying to optimize your websiteâs dashboard. Your goal is to increase user signups. Your team designs four different layouts: A, B, C, and D.
You run an A/B/n test. Users are randomly assigned to one of the four layouts and you track their activity. Your hypothesis is:
layout influences signup behavior
.
You plan ship the winner if the p-value for one of the layout choices falls below the conventional threshold of 0.05.
Then you check the results:
Option B looks best. p = 0.041. It floats to the top as if inviting action. The team is satisfied and ships it.
But the logic beneath the 0.05 cutoff is more fragile than it appears. That threshold assumes youâre testing a single variant. But you tested four. That alone
increases
the odds of a false positive.
Letâs look at what that actually means.
Setting a p-value threshold of 0.05 is equivalent to saying:

And that risk scales quickly. The more variants you test, the higher the odds that something looks like a win just by coincidence. Statistically, the probability of at least one false positive increases with each additional test, converging toward 1 as the number of comparisons grows:

44341281.article_content:
Requiem for a Solar Plant
The email landed like a brick through a plate glass window.
"...requiring reconductoring of 1.71 miles at a cost of $795,150...limiting output to 3MW..."
I stared at my laptop screen, the blue light illuminating the shadows under my eyes in my darkened California living room. Outside, endless February rain tapped against the windows like impatient fingers. My gut churned, a familiar discomfort that had become my constant companion over the past year. This wasn't just bad news. This was a death sentence.
Three years of work. Over a million dollars spent. A team scattered across three continents. All of it now threatened by two pages of engineering assessments and a single number: 3MW. My solar plant, originally planned for 4.54MW, had just been slashed by a third. The economics that had barely made sense before now collapsed entirely.
I reached for my phone and typed out a message to Mr. R.
Just saw the interconnection report. We need to talk.
The reply came quickly, despite the eleven-hour time difference. Mr. R had an uncanny ability to be available whenever needed, as though he never slept.
I've been reviewing the numbers. It doesn't work.
I rubbed my temples, remembering the day years earlier when the Invictus Solar project had first crystallized in my mind—a perfect convergence of opportunity and purpose. I'd made a fortune by accident in cryptocurrency, more money than I'd ever dreamed of, and had been searching for something meaningful to do with it. Something that would generate sustainable returns while helping shift the world toward renewable energy.
The tax advantages alone had seemed almost too good to be true: stack the federal Investment Tax Credit for solar with the capital gains deferrals from the Qualified Opportunity Zone program, and you could turn marginal economics into attractive returns. It was financial alchemy—transforming crypto profits into clean energy infrastructure while minimizing tax exposure.
Financial Projections (Pre-Interconnection Study)
- Total Installed Cost: $8,723,136 ($1.37/Watt DC)
- Capacity: 6375 kW DC / 4540 kW AC
- Net Capacity Factor: 23.8%
- Pre-tax IRR: -0.92%
- After-tax Equity IRR: 2.56%
- NPV: ($1,499,388) at 6% discount rate
- QOZ Tax Benefits: Estimated to add 3.7% to IRR
These projections relied on a $45/MWh PPA price and assumed 4.54MW AC capacity.
The reduction to 3MW in the interconnection study would significantly worsen these already-marginal returns.
Now, eighteen months later, sitting in my living room staring at the brutal economics of my failed project, I wondered how something so promising had gone so terribly wrong.
My phone rang. Mr. R.
"The land was good. The solar analysis was good. The land was flat. The price was right. The goddamn opportunity zone lined up perfectly," Mr. R said, his Russian accent more pronounced than usual, betraying his frustration. "But Texas with it's insane mineral rights and the interconnection study…"
I smiled despite myself. There was something comforting about Mr. R's exasperation, as though his anger could somehow shield us both from the disappointment.
"Tell me again what they're saying," I said, reaching for a notepad. "The whole thing."
"They want to limit us to three megawatts instead of four point five. They want us to pay nearly eight hundred thousand just to upgrade their wires. Another hundred and forty thousand for two reclosers. Plus tax." Mr. R spoke with the precision of someone who had memorized every painful detail. "And even with all that, they still say there will be fault current violations. So they cut our capacity anyway."
"Because the substation is too far away."
"Four point six miles instead of the one or two we thought. The distribution circuit takes a winding path we couldn't see from the satellite images. It goes to an entirely different substation. It's not just the distance though, our neighbors on the line have 'noisy usage' "
I stared at the ceiling, my mind racing through alternatives. Could we negotiate with the power company? Find another interconnection point? Redesign the system to work with the reduced capacity?
But I already knew the answers. We had spent months on these problems already. There was no alternative interconnection point on the property. The reduced capacity made the economics impossible. The numbers simply didn't work anymore.
"So that's it then," I said softly. "We shut it down."
The line went quiet for a moment.
"Yes," Mr. R finally said. "We shut it down. But first, I calculate exactly how much money we have wasted."
The Assembling
It started with a whiteboard session in my Palo Alto home in the summer of 2022, my kid running about in his underwear as I scribbled numbers and scenarios. Cryptocurrency had been an unexpected windfall for me, but I was painfully aware of the ecological footprint of mining. Moreover I squirmed at the 32.3% capital gains tax.
California has an extra 12.3% on top of the 20% for federal long term capital

data.title: Type Inference Zoo
data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个互动式的在线编程 playground，用户可以在浏览器中直接尝试类型推断示例并探索各种算法。该平台旨在简化动手实践的过程，适合学习者通过实际操作来理解编程概念和算法逻辑，无需配置本地环境，便捷直观。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bruno Oliveira研究小组的工作量以及一种名为CP的编程语言的特点和优势

不同观点：
• dmkolobov认为Bruno Oliveira的研究小组产出了大量工作，并提到了一种具有不相交交集和联合类型的语言CP，提供了一个GitHub链接供进一步了解。

• b0a04gl对Python在类型系统建模中的应用感到有趣，指出Python本身并不严格执行类型，但这种特性在进行某些底层实现时反而成为优势。具体而言，Python不需要与编译器层斗争或处理多余的细节，可以直接构建推理逻辑、决定类型的统一方式及上下文的存储等。这种无注释和无转换的特性让开发者可以专注于核心逻辑，有助于更好地理解理论。

• flashgordon对CP语言表示赞赏，并提到自己一直想进行类似的项目但未能成功，对该项目的实现表示钦佩。

补充讨论：
• b0a04gl特别强调了Python在处理类型系统建模时的独特优势，即语言本身的简洁性和灵活性使得开发者能够更专注于核心问题，而不被语言本身的限制所困扰。

• 争议的焦点可能在于动态类型语言如Python在类型系统建模中的适用性。虽然Python不严格执行类型，但这种特性在某些研究和开发场景中反而成为优势，使得开发者可以更自由地实现复杂的逻辑。

• 不同语言在类型系统建模中的优劣成为讨论中的一个隐含主题，特别是Python的灵活性与传统静态类型语言的对比。

data.title: Compiler for the B Programming Language
data.author: ycuser2
data.article_summary: 该项目是一个由Rust实现的B编程语言编译器，名为"b"。目前编译器尚未完全实现。项目依赖Rust和fasm（用作后端编译器），用户可以通过`make`命令编译项目并运行示例代码。项目包含`btest`工具用于自动化测试，支持按平台和测试用例进行筛选测试。B语言的更多信息可参考相关链接。项目采用MIT许可证，目前有368个星标和54个分支。

B Programming Language

Logo by Strawberry 🍓
Compiler for the B Programming Language implemented in
Crust
Dependencies
Rust
- the compiler is written in it;
fasm

Quick Start
$
make
$
./build/b -run ./examples/hello_world.b
Also check out more examples at
./examples/
.
Testing
The project comes with
btest
utility which tests the B compiler. It is built automatically along with the B compiler when you do
make
.
When you run it, it just builds and runs all the tests from the
./tests/
folder on all the supported targets and generates a matrix report. Give it a try to see it for yourself:
$ make
$ ./build/btest
It doesn't crash when it encounters errors, it just collects the statuses of the tests on all the platforms to give an overview of the current state of the compiler.
Slicing the Test Matrix
If you want to test only on a specific platform you can supply the flag
-t
$
./build/btest -t fasm-x86_64-linux
You can supply several platforms
$
./build/btest -t fasm-x86_64-linux -t uxn
If you want to run a specific test case you can supply flag
-c
$
./build/btest -c upper
You can do several tests
$
./build/btest -c upper -c vector
And of course you can combine both
-c
and
-t
flags to slice the Test Matrix however you want
$
./build/btest -c upper -c vector -t fasm-x86_64-linux -t uxn

data.article_summary: Luna Rail正在开发新一代昼夜火车，旨在优化空间利用、提升舒适度并兼顾经济性，提供比航空更环保的出行选择。其核心技术包括“酒店舱”和“座位舱”，前者为单人私密舱，白天可作起居室或移动办公室，夜间转换为舒适大床；后者为白天大座椅，夜间可平躺。通过物理模型和用户测试不断优化设计，测试显示多数用户认为这两种舱体比高铁二等座甚至一等座更具吸引力。技术目标是最大化车厢容量，使夜火车更具竞争力，并推动票价降低和线路扩展。Luna Rail还提供统一设计的应用程序，管理预订、信息和舱内控制等全程服务。

data.title: Don't Read This If You Have a Security Clearance (2023)
data.author: greyface-
data.article_summary:
1969年，克格勃成功进行了一次 clever 的欺骗行动，通过在美国真实战争计划泄露中夹杂伪造文件，试图挑拨美国与北约盟友的关系。50多年后，作者提议在美国情报机构的培训中使用1969年泄露事件作为识别伪造文件的练习，但被官员拒绝，因为这些材料仍可能被归类为机密。尽管这些文件自我们出生前就已公开，情报人员仍不允许查看。

2013年，爱德华·斯诺登事件后，五角大楼发布新规，要求员工若发现可能属于机密的信息，必须立即报告。此规定旨在防止员工故意寻找或传播这些信息，违者将受制裁。这项政策让联邦雇员或承包商在看新闻、浏览社交媒体、搜索谷歌甚至读书时都面临风险。

尽管这些泄露有时会导致重大地缘政治问题或危及生命，但也提供了丰富的资料，帮助专家理解美国及其对手的间谍技术。然而，美国政府禁止安全机构人员查看这些已公开的泄露文件，即便公众和敌对国家已在研究它们，这显得荒谬。特别是在2016年Shadow Brokers泄露后，国防部网络防御人员面临无法研究对手使用NSA黑客工具的困境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于处理泄密信息和安全保密政策的争议

不同观点：
• Zak认为，禁止确认或否认泄密信息的政策是有道理的，但一旦信息被公开，再假装 otherwise 是荒谬的。
• ggm提出，应减少对普通事实的安全分类，降低敏感性，并质疑安全设施（SCIF）在信息管理上的实质性改进。
• anonymousiam以其40年的安全保密经验指出，未解密的文件应继续受到访问控制，即使是持有保密许可的人，未经授权访问也是违规行为。
• mmsc对泄密信息的真实性和完整性提出质疑，认为可能缺少重要背景或被编辑。
• mrlatinos以讽刺口吻表示，付费墙可以保护公众免受泄密信息的影响。
• helsinkiandrew以讽刺方式提问，是否通过散布泄密信息可以保护自己的隐私。
• atlgator指出，保密政策适用于所有持有保密许可的人，而不仅仅是国防部员工。
• bell-cot批评文章对政策的简单化攻击，强调泄密问题的根源在于机构防止泄密的能力不足，并指出解密决策的复杂性和潜在风险。

补充讨论：
• 关于解密过程的复杂性和实际操作中的困难，bell-cot指出解密决定由职业国家安全人员做出，且历史上没有人因解密信息而获得晋升。
• 对互联网环境和公众反应的担忧，bell-cot认为解密信息可能会引发不必要的公众恐慌和误解。
• 讨论中还涉及到对学术界在国家安全政策讨论中的角色和责任的质疑，特别是对那些只关注自身不便而不考虑全局改进的学者。

争议焦点：
• 保密政策的合理性和有效性。
• 解密过程的实际操作和潜在风险。
• 泄密信息对公众和国家安全的影响。

这些观点展示了在处理泄密信息和保密政策上的多方面争议，包括实际操作、政策效果以及学术和公众讨论的责任。

44341676.article_content:
I
n 1969, the KGB
pulled off one of the cleverest deceptions of the Cold War, slipping forged documents into a leak of otherwise authentic U.S. war plans in an effort to pit America against its NATO allies. More than 50 years later, I was invited to run a training session on disinformation for a U.S. intelligence agency. In my back-and-forth with the official in charge, I proposed a game of spot-the-fake using the 1969 leak. The exercise would test whether the intelligence officers could recognize one of the best forgeries in the history of spycraft. But the official shot down my idea. The leaked material technically may still be classified, he explained, so we weren’t allowed to use it. In fact, although the documents had been sitting in public view since before most of us were born, the officers in the class weren’t even allowed to look at them.
For this I had the Department of Defense to thank. On June 7, 2013, days after the Edward Snowden story broke, the Pentagon
issued
an immediate security guidance: Employees or contractors “who inadvertently discover potentially classified information in the public domain shall report its existence immediately to their Security Manager,” read the new rule. This reporting requirement was onerous enough on its own to scare federal employees. To make things worse, those who didn’t just stumble across classified documents but looked for them deliberately would be punished: Contractors or employees “who seek out classified information in the public domain, acknowledge its accuracy or existence, or proliferate the information in any way will be subject to sanctions,” stated the notice. (The directive was grounded in a similar
2010 rule
issued by the Office of Management and Budget.) Given that the Snowden revelations were being published by media organizations and blasted around the internet, the policy effectively turned mundane activities like watching the news, browsing social media, searching Google, and even reading books into a risky proposition for any federal employee or contractor.
Ten years later, the illogic of this policy has only grown clearer. In the pre-internet age, leaks of classified documents were rare. Today, thanks to the internet, they’re regular events. The names of the leaks are infamous in national-security circles:
Cablegate
in 2010, enabled by Chelsea Manning; the
Snowden

episode

release

, courtesy of Jack Teixeira.
These leaks can cause major geopolitical headaches. They can even get people killed. But, like the KGB leak of 1969, they also provide rich troves of material that advance expert understanding of how tradecraft is conducted—by both the U.S. and its adversaries. Snowden exposed how intelligence agencies adjusted their methods to the digital era, how signals-intelligence development evolved, and much more. The Shadow Brokers and Vault 7 exposed how implant platforms are designed and how the NSA does digital counterintelligence. The Discord leaks revealed invaluable knowledge on a range of geopolitical crises. It is simply impossible to understand the story of technical spycraft and computer-network penetrations in the 21st century—a discipline that first emerged in secret—without studying these unauthorized disclosures.

If a government official denies a certain element of a leak, for example, they are implicitly affirming the rest of it. 1969年，克格勃成功进行了一次 clever 的欺骗行动，通过在美国真实战争计划泄露中夹杂伪造文件，试图挑拨美国与北约盟友的关系。50多年后，作者提议在美国情报机构的培训中使用1969年泄露事件作为识别伪造文件的练习，但被官员拒绝，因为这些材料仍可能被归类为机密。尽管这些文件自我们出生前就已公开，情报人员仍不允许查看。

2013年，爱德华·斯诺登事件后，五角大楼发布新规，要求员工若发现可能属于机密的信息，必须立即报告。此规定旨在防止员工故意寻找或传播这些信息，违者将受制裁。这项政策让联邦雇员或承包商在看新闻、浏览社交媒体、搜索谷歌甚至读书时都面临风险。

尽管这些泄露有时会导致重大地缘政治问题或危及生命，但也提供了丰富的资料，帮助专家理解美国及其对手的间谍技术。然而，美国政府禁止安全机构人员查看这些已公开的泄露文件，即便公众和敌对国家已在研究它们，这显得荒谬。特别是在2016年Shadow Brokers泄露后，国防部网络防御人员面临无法研究对手使用NSA黑客工具的困境。

data.title: Axolotls May Hold the Key to Regrowing Limbs
data.author: noleary
data.article_summary: Axolotls, a type of salamander capable of regrowing missing body parts, are helping scientists uncover the secrets of limb regeneration. In a study published in *Nature Communications*, researchers led by James Monaghan from Northeastern University genetically engineered axolotls to glow and tracked the molecular pathways involved in regeneration. They discovered that retinoic acid, a vitamin A derivative, plays a crucial role in determining which type of limb should regrow, with higher concentrations leading to more extensive regrowth. The enzyme CYP26B1 controls retinoic acid levels, while the *Shox* gene is essential for proper limb regeneration. Axolotls share these genetic pathways with humans, suggesting potential for future applications in human medicine, such as developing treatments to regenerate limbs rather than form scar tissue. Though human limb regeneration is still far off, foundational research like this is crucial for progress.
